payload.feature:
Close issue #231: a promoted capability spec does not name the change that wrote it, so the trail runs one way. The operator ruled this on 2026-09-06 and it is recorded as an addendum to decision 0042 (PR #232); this run is the enactment.

Read the issue, decision 0042 with its addendum, and the first change to complete the machine, `2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i`, which promoted eight capabilities and names itself in none of them.

**The ruling, already accepted, in the operator's words:** the archive step appends one `## Provenance` line per capability it touched, appended and never rewritten, and pre-ruling archives are backfilled once by the enacting slice.

**Build it so:**

1. **The dialect's `archive` instruction does the appending.** It is the step that folds a change into standing truth, so it is the step that records which change wrote which capability. One line per capability the change touched, appended to that capability's spec; existing provenance lines are never rewritten or reordered, because standing truth accumulates and does not get edited into a different meaning.
2. **The backfill happens once, in this slice**, over the archives that predate the ruling — `2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i` and any other archived change — so every promoted capability names at least one change from the day this lands.
3. **A test that every capability's provenance list is non-empty and resolves**: each named change exists under the archive, and no capability is left without one. That test is what keeps the trail two-way after this slice.
4. **Rationale is not duplicated into standing truth.** A provenance line is a pointer, not a summary: it names the change and nothing else. The whole point of decision 0042's two-directory model is that the why lives in the change and the truth lives in the spec.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Do not push and do not open a pull request; the operator lands it. Say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

Reviewed the whole delivery at the MERGED head ca7e5a3 (0513205, 478d9a6 and the three reconciling merges a1ef3e3/f11ea0f/ca7e5a3), i.e. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` = 26 files. Earlier review passes covered only 0513205 and 0513205..478d9a6, so the merge reconciliation with #245/#248/#246 is reviewed here for the first time.

CORRECTNESS. The enactment matches decision 0042's addendum of 2026-09-06 ruling by ruling. Ruling 1: the appending lives in the dialect's archive step -- `dialects/openspec.json` gains `archive.instructions: "openspec/archive.md"`, the file is dialect data (not a hard-coded path), it joins `instruction_paths` so it passes the same spelling-only relative-path gate and is pinned by `Dialect::load`/`render` into `rendered["implement"]`, and a resume takes the prompt from the pin rather than re-reading a mutable file. spec-kit keeps `archive: unsupported` and carries no instruction; `check` refuses a v3 command archive that names none. Ruling 2 / backfill: exactly 8 archived deltas, 8 living capabilities, one appended line each, all `- `2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i` -- folded 2026-09-06`, pointer only, no rationale copied. Test: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs` walks BOTH directions -- specs->archive (non-empty, resolves, the named change really touched the capability) and archive->specs (a fold that promoted a delta and skipped the append fails, which the one-way walk the binding asked for would pass) -- and `named_change` holds the line to one backticked name, ` -- folded `, a bare YYYY-MM-DD and nothing after, so "a pointer, not a summary" is tested rather than asserted. The v1/v2 pin-reading widening in 478d9a6 is correct and correctly placed: the version is read from the raw bytes before deserialization, so an unread version is refused BY ITS VERSION instead of as an untagged-variant mismatch; each version is held to its own shape (`tool.install` absent at v1, required from v2; archive `instructions` absent below v3, required at v3); a FILE stays v3-only so the requirement cannot be escaped by writing an older label. `tool.install` becoming `Option` is inert -- grep confirms no production consumer outside dialect.rs.

MERGE RECONCILIATION (new ground). #245 added `completion.md` and updated two deltas inside the SAME archived directory rather than creating a new one, so no additional provenance line is owed. Both living specs it touched (`boundary-readouts`, `gate-boundary-policy`) took main's new requirement text ABOVE the `## Provenance` section, which the test requires to be the last `## ` heading; verified in the merged files. #248's doctor rewrite and #246's adapter work merged without touching the dialect surface.

CONSTRAINTS. No frozen byte moved: contracts v1/v2, realms, seat-record, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/` and `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson` are unchanged; `dialect.v3.schema.json` lands beside them and is pinned by frozen_contracts.rs. The two dialect trees are byte-identical (`diff dialects/openspec/archive.md crates/brokkr-cli/dialects/openspec/archive.md` -> identical). No new test drives a boxed step. No witness or compose digest moved (witness/packaging suites green).

SIMPLICITY. Nothing overbuilt. `check_command_tokens` was restructured from a chained iterator to a (argv, state) vector only because the archive arm now has its own type; that is the minimum change, not a rewrite.

SECURITY: none. The pin reader accepting older `schema` labels grants no new power -- a manifest tamperer already controls the pinned `content` and the whole `rendered` map, so a downgrade buys nothing, and the FILE surface stays fail-closed at v3 so no v2 label can be written today to shed the instruction requirement. The new instruction path is gated identically to every existing one, read once at pin time, and covered by the dialect pin's sha256. Info only, not introduced here: an instruction path may still be a symlink whose target content is rendered into a model prompt and pinned into the manifest -- a pre-existing property of all seven instruction paths, unchanged by this slice.

EVIDENCE I RAN MYSELF on merged HEAD ca7e5a3 (a clean tree): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 0, 65 suites 'test result: ok', 1391 tests, zero FAILED (log at .forge/review-test.log); `cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify` both exit 0. This is the first green run recorded ON the merge; prior passes ran on 478d9a6.

THREE LOW RESIDUALS, none returned, none security.

1. low, correctness/instruction-fidelity -- `dialects/openspec/archive.md:14` and its byte-identical twin `crates/brokkr-cli/dialects/openspec/archive.md:14`. The one artifact whose job is to state the line's shape states it wrong: it is a single-backtick code span containing backslash-escaped backticks, `- \`<archived-directory-name>\` -- folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Backslash escapes are inert inside a CommonMark code span and `prompt_for` hands the file to the smith as raw trimmed text, so the smith is shown a template with literal backslashes. A smith copying it faithfully writes a line that `named_change` (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs:36) refuses at `strip_prefix("- `")` -- the fold's own instruction can generate the shape the gate rejects. It fails loudly in this repo, so it is low, but for any other realm adopting this dialect the rule is prose-only with no gate behind it. Fix: the fenced ```text block that provenance.rs's own doc comment already uses. Carried unchanged from the previous review pass; still present at HEAD.

2. low, documentation/governance -- `docs/decisions/0042-the-council-is-brokkrs-the-dialect-is-the-realms.md:573-575`. Ruling 3's enforcement binding still ends 'This build reads `brokkr.dialect/v2` only, which costs nothing today: the dialect landed the same day with no realm declaring one, so no journal pins a v1 dialect for a resume to reload.' After this slice a FILE reads v3 only and a PIN reads v1/v2/v3, and 478d9a6's own commit message records that the stated reason 'was never true'. An accepted decision now contradicts shipped code with no marker, in a realm whose premise is that decisions are authoritative. The repo has the mechanism (the `## Erratum` heading on decision 0043, itself pinned by openspec/specs/boundary-guides/spec.md). The implementer correctly declined to edit an accepted decision, so this is an operator ruling, not a return. `contracts/README.md` and `docs/guides/versioning.md` both record the file-versus-pin split correctly, so the prose elsewhere is consistent.

3. low, unverified-interaction (a risk I could not resolve, not a defect I demonstrated) -- nobody across three review passes has run OpenSpec itself against a spec carrying the new section. Two questions are open: (a) does `openspec validate --archived --strict --no-interactive`, which IS this dialect's own verify command, tolerate an unrecognised `## Provenance` section at the end of a living spec.md? If not, every subsequent SDD run's verify step reddens on the self realm. (b) does `openspec archive` regenerate `openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md` from its parsed requirement model? If it does, a later fold would delete the provenance lines already there before the smith appends the new one, and 'appended and never rewritten' would not be structurally achievable by this design -- it would fail loudly on the next run (the archive->specs walk would find a missing name), but it would fail. Either answer turning out badly raises this to medium. I could not check: `openspec` is installed at /home/vyanakiev/.volta/bin/openspec but the seat sandbox refuses to execute it and refuses to read anything outside the worktree, so I could neither run it nor read its source. One `openspec validate --archived --strict --no-interactive` on this tree, plus one look at whether archive rewrites or edits spec.md, closes it -- worth doing before this lands.

ALSO COULD NOT VERIFY: the exact-coverage gate. `scripts/coverage-exact.sh` cannot be run from a seat (script execution is refused), so I have no measured number for the new branches in dialect.rs; the implementer's recorded report (.forge/cov) reads 21399/21399 lines, 3350/3350 branches, 2028/2028 functions, but it predates the last source edit and predates all three merges, so CI must supply this. I also could not read issue #231 directly (no GitHub access this session); I reviewed against decision 0042's addendum, which I read in full, and the task framing, which restate the ruling.
